answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using zero-knowledge credential nullifiers. Behind a velvet mask of ZK-SNARK privacy, an agent proves it holds an issuer-signed key and derives a deterministic epoch nullifier, like a single-use quill, letting verifiers block duplicates without exposing the signer. Attackers incur the verifiable cost of obtaining a vetted credential, scarce as saffron, per identity. However, a compromised or colluding issuer can still mint fake accounts undetected.
